parallel.requirements: Recognized the broad Mootdx package requirement and especially the need for a complete installable pyproject, unified exports, Reader/Quotes/Affair APIs, CLI commands, docs, samples, fixtures, and tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Despite swarm mode, the main actor kept all work, chose to reuse the authentic 0.11.7 PyPI/GitHub source, and performed all integration, patching, and verification itself.
parallel.implementation: Downloaded the wheel and sdist, cloned GitHub v0.11.7, verified source equality, copied the full repo into /workspace, then patched pyproject dependencies, __init__ exports, utils holiday exports, contrib Path, DownloadTDXCaiWu, and Customize behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a full upstream-like tree including package, docs, samples, tests, fixtures, scripts, and packaging files; final answer summarized the completed implementation and checks.
parallel.verification: Ran install/import smoke checks, the upstream test suite twice with 87 passed and 56 skipped, CLI help checks, module import checks, workflow checks, and a structure check before final response.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 14 of 92 cases, likely reflecting gaps hidden from the local checks; however the trajectory reached closure with a complete-looking project and no timeout.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same broad requirements and attempted to implement core modules, financial tools, server management, CLI, pyproject, tests, cache, utils, demjson, and fixture-based readers from scratch.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single serial main actor owned every module and used a TodoList to track large categories of work; no child or parallel work was used.
serial.implementation: Hand-wrote many source files and tests, including a large custom demjson.py and minimal fixture generation, then patched discovered bugs such as demjson -Infinity handling, tdxpy logger import, socket import, and fzline lookup.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Produced a smaller generated package with build artifacts and limited tests/fixtures, but did not deliver the full docs/sample/fixture/test tree required by the prompt before cancellation.
serial.verification: Ran self-authored pytest tests to 73 passed, then attempted package import and reader fixture smoke checks; import and reader checks exposed failures, one fzline fix was applied, but there was no final successful whole-task verification after that edit.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out/cancelled at an active step after the fzline edit, with no final answer; official evaluation failed 53 tests and had 1 error.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized that the prompt closely matched Mootdx 0.11.7 and covered package metadata, API exports, docs, tests, fixtures, CLI, and workflows by importing the full upstream tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same broad requirement list but translated it into a manually generated reduced implementation and smaller self-authored tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel covered more of the specified repository surface by source reuse; serial covered the main API categories but omitted much of the full upstream structure and behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel mode entered swarm mode but made a single-owner decision: copy the upstream repo and handle patches, tests, and finalization in the main actor.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one main actor with a TodoList splitting work by module families but kept all writing and fixes under that actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither used true delegation; the main difference was upstream reuse versus broad manual implementation, not parallel decomposition.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: With no child briefs or handoffs, interface context stayed inside one actor; the main actor patched exports and compatibility based on direct smoke-test failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial similarly had no inter-agent handoffs, but had to infer many library interfaces while hand-writing modules, leading to discovered import and reader interface failures late in the run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no cross-agent context boundary; serial had ordinary local API-mismatch defects, while parallel relied on upstream interfaces and patched fewer mismatches.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel downloaded Mootdx 0.11.7 artifacts, verified sdist and GitHub repo equality, copied the full repo, then made narrow compatibility/spec edits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial hand-wrote source files module-by-module, including core, utils, cache, financial, tools, contrib, server, CLI, pyproject, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel delivered a complete upstream-derived implementation; serial delivered a bespoke approximation with higher defect risk and narrower coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reached an end-turn final answer that summarized implementation and verification, and the status recorded a completed prompt outcome.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial was interrupted/cancelled after applying a reader fzline edit and did not produce a final completion response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closed and presented a deliverable; serial remained in an active repair loop when the run ended.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated by syncing the full GitHub tree, removing .git, and then editing specific package files in the same workspace under one owner.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated many newly written files plus generated build artifacts and a reduced fixture/test tree under one owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's final tree was broad and provenance-consistent from upstream; serial's final tree was locally generated and less complete, but neither shows concurrent write collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran upstream tests to 87 passed/56 skipped, checked CLI commands, imported all modules, verified workflow examples, and did a structure check.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran its own tests to 73 passed, but later import and reader smoke checks failed, and after the final fzline patch no successful full verification or acceptance occurred before cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had broader, successful local verification aligned to the upstream project; serial had narrower self-tests and unresolved late-stage acceptance risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in about 965 agent seconds and 1122 cell seconds without timeout, leaving enough time for final checks and final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial consumed the full budget, timed out/cancelled after about 2409 agent seconds and 2458 cell seconds, and had no final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's upstream reuse preserved budget and closure; serial's manual build consumed the run and ended under cancellation pressure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official outcomes are failures from the current completed cell/status.json evaluation, so there is no pass/fail-discordant outcome. The material score gap is still concrete: parallel used the real upstream Mootdx 0.11.7 codebase and finished with broader local tests and final delivery, while serial manually built an incomplete approximation, encountered late import and reader failures, and was cancelled before a final verified closure.
parallel_contributors: Copied full upstream Mootdx 0.11.7 repo and fixtures after verifying PyPI/GitHub source equality.
Ran broader upstream tests, CLI checks, import checks, workflow checks, and a structure check before final response.
Completed without timeout and produced a final answer.
serial_contributors: Hand-authored many modules and tests from scratch, leaving narrower coverage than the upstream tree.
Late smoke checks still failed around package imports and fzline/fixture handling.
Timed out/cancelled before a final post-fix verification and final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel upstream reuse versus serial manual approximation is an ordinary implementation strategy difference, not a concurrency label.
Serial's late fixture and reader errors are ordinary implementation defects and budget/closure issues, not parallel coordination failures.
evaluator_effects: Mounted evaluation summaries provide counts but not individual hidden-test failure names, so the score-gap explanation relies on trajectory evidence plus official counts.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative explanation for score gap, not an outcome-differential concurrency root cause
